mode: bounded scientific test; canonical decisions preserved
title: SCFA Production & Signalling
mission: Maintain short-chain fatty acid production and signalling that supports gut barrier and brain communication.
identity_verdict: confirmed: SCFAs include butyrate; no separate butyrate-only PM inferred

ownership.PM5: microbial substrate conversion into SCFAs and resulting SCFA actions
ownership.PM4: upstream substrate-processing ecology and selection, not interchangeable with production output
ownership.PM1: downstream epithelial barrier operation; not a dietary butyrate-production claim

propositions.question: Do defined fermentable substrates supply microbial SCFA-producing capacity?
propositions.limits: Substrate structure, donor ecology, degrader/producer cross-feeding and compartment matter; not every fibre raises faecal butyrate.

propositions.question: Do SCFAs engage host barrier/metabolic signalling?
propositions.limits: Different acids, tissues and concentrations; no generic dietary or cognitive benefit.

propositions.question: Do these foods improve human brain function or ADHD through butyrate production?
propositions.decision: unresolved; not established by reviewed corpus
propositions.limits: No tested end-to-end dietary mediation. Do not use faecal concentrations or cell studies as clinical evidence.

evidence_inventory.decision: Supports preparation-specific substrate provision; faecal endpoints, not brain efficacy. Potato RS2 increased faecal butyrate; maize RS2 and chicory inulin did not significantly increase that endpoint. Specialist degrader/producer associations constrain cross-feeding interpretation.

Site-specific constraints are essential: no detected distal-ileal fermentation; proximal-colon concentrations rose in one sampled person. Separately infused labelled SCFAs established host handling, not labelled FOS/GOS-to-butyrate conversion.
Mechanistic synthesis, not an independent primary fermentation experiment. Retain as synthesis; structure and donor constraints remain.
Propionate-related brain-endothelial mechanisms support downstream plausibility, not butyrate-specific dietary efficacy.
Butyrate altered mitochondrial responses in lymphoblastoid cells; concentration, redox state and cell phenotype matter. No human dietary or cognitive outcome.
Keep contextual: faecal associations do not establish microbial production rate, causality or ADHD treatment efficacy.
Pathway context; not independent primary replication or proof of a food-to-brain effect.

Twelve participants received inulin; isotope-dilution estimates support SCFA formation. Colonic output estimates depend on assumed systemic availability. This does not contradict a null faecal butyrate change or establish a brain effect.
Purified citrus pectin fermented in cultures from three donors with acetate/butyrate formation. Does not establish whole-apple or human brain effects.
Pectin isolation/characterisation across thirteen apple cultivars supports qualitative food supply; no total-fibre-to-pectin quantity conversion.
Chemical characterisation of extracted chicory-root inulin supports identity and source presence. Extraction yield/purity is not an edible-food concentration.

material_issues.finding: The named resistant-potato-starch lever receives generic resistant-starch food-class targets, including non-potato foods and a cooked/cooled material. Composition verification does not establish the tested potato-RS2 exposure.

The FOS/GOS extraction omits intestinal-site null results and does not distinguish separately infused SCFA tracers from substrate-derived production. Its broad positive summary needs qualification, not blanket rejection of fermentation.
Pascale is a systematic review of in-vitro studies, not another primary cellular experiment.

scoring: No CC/SEC factors, scores or anchors assigned or altered.
